description:
SURFACED by PR #149 / CI run 34710897082 with RUST_TEST_THREADS=4. The parallel fixture matrix opened enough readiness pipes that FZ_EXEC_READY_FD became 10. Four static harness tests execute sh snippets using dynamic redirection through eval, for example eval "exec ${FZ_EXEC_READY_FD}>&-" and eval "printf x >&${FZ_EXEC_READY_FD}". On Ubuntu Actions /bin/sh is dash; after expansion it reports `sh: 1: exec: 10: not found` because dash only parses a literal single-digit redirect before expansion. Serial RUST_TEST_THREADS=1 hid the invalid contract by keeping descriptors below 10.

Goal: make readiness-probe controls descriptor-number agnostic, with no shell-specific dynamic-redirection grammar. Pass the ready descriptor through an executable-safe mechanism or write/close it in Rust-owned probes; preserve the probes exact lifecycle assertions, process-group semantics, and bounded capture behavior. Add a regression that exercises a multi-digit fd on Linux. Verify the four historical tests plus the default-parallel fixture matrix under cargo llvm-cov on Ubuntu. This blocks fz-qds.
title: Fixture readiness probes must support multi-digit file descriptors
